# SPE Round r01 Plan: Triage Agent

The spec is your prompt: "triage tickets correctly and cheaply." This plan is the r01 prediction. After you approve it, I record the prediction, build the agent and harness, and run one Workflow as the eval. I make a local commit after each step. I do not push.

## Defaults I chose

Your prompt leaves several things open. I chose a default for each one. Each default goes into `spe/spec/disagreements.md` with you as owner.

| ID | Open point | Default for r01 |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | Ticket domain | Customer support tickets for a B2B SaaS product |
| D2 | What "triage" outputs | One category and one priority per ticket, plus a one-line reason, as JSON |
| D3 | Category set | billing, bug, account_access, feature_request, how_to, outage |
| D4 | Priority set | P1 (urgent) to P4 (low) |
| D5 | Data | Synthetic tickets, because no real tickets exist. A separate Opus subagent writes them from a label guide. It never sees the agent prompts. |
| D6 | "Correctly" | Category accuracy of at least 0.85 and P1 recall of at least 0.90 |
| D7 | "Cheaply" | The winner is the cheapest config that meets D6. I do not set a dollar ceiling, because you have not given one. |
| D8 | Data split | A 20-ticket dev set for prompt building and a 120-ticket held-out eval set. I never tune prompts on the eval set. |

Two decisions only you can make stay open: real tickets to replace D5, and a dollar ceiling for D7.

## Specify

This table goes into `spe/spec/spec.md` under "Round r01".

| ID | Requirement | Source | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | The agent assigns one category from D3 to each ticket | User: "triage tickets" | Code: label exactly matches gold |
| R2 | The agent assigns one priority from D4 to each ticket | User: "triage tickets" | Code: label exactly matches gold |
| R3 | Category accuracy is at least 0.85 | User: "correctly", default D6 | Code: mean of R1 matches over the eval set |
| R4 | P1 recall is at least 0.90, because a missed urgent ticket costs the most | User: "correctly", default D6 | Code: share of gold P1 tickets labeled P1 |
| R5 | Output is valid JSON matching the schema | Decision: graders need structured output | Code: JSON schema validator |
| R6 | The reason quotes or paraphrases the ticket text | Decision: a reason should be traceable to the ticket | Judge: Opus subagent, blind to config |
| R7 | Cost per ticket is measured and compared across configs | User: "cheaply", default D7 | Code: API usage tokens times the price sheet read at run time |

Round r01 has no earlier proposals to adopt or reject.

## Predict

**Configurations.** Each config changes one thing from its parent.

| Config | Parent | The one change |
|---|---|---|
| C1 | none | Sonnet-tier model, zero-shot prompt with label definitions |
| C2 | C1 | Haiku-tier model instead of Sonnet-tier |
| C3 | C2 | Adds 8 few-shot examples from the dev set |

In step 0, I read the exact model IDs and prices from current Anthropic docs and pin them in the yaml.

**Numbers.** A hit means the measured value falls inside the band. Round r01 has no earlier round, so `same_as_last_round` is "n/a". The naive guess to beat is "C2 and C3 score the same as C1".

| Metric | C1 | C2 | C3 | Grader check | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| M1 Category accuracy | 0.87 ± 0.05 | 0.80 ± 0.06 | 0.86 ± 0.05 | `grade.mjs` exact match to `gold.category` | Six categories are well separated. A smaller model confuses bug with outage and how_to with feature_request. Examples fix most of that. |
| M2 Priority accuracy | 0.70 ± 0.08 | 0.62 ± 0.08 | 0.68 ± 0.08 | `grade.mjs` exact match to `gold.priority` | Priority is subjective, so P2 and P3 often swap. |
| M3 P1 recall | 0.92 ± 0.06 | 0.84 ± 0.08 | 0.90 ± 0.07 | `grade.mjs` recall on gold P1 | Outage words are clear signals, but a smaller model under-calls urgency. |
| M4 Schema-valid rate | 0.99 ± 0.01 | 0.97 ± 0.02 | 0.99 ± 0.01 | `schema.mjs` validator | Examples show the exact JSON shape. |
| M5 Mean tokens per ticket | 650 ± 120 | 650 ± 120 | 1500 ± 250 | API `usage` fields summed | The prompt length is the same for C1 and C2. Eight examples add about 850 tokens. |
| M6 Cost per ticket relative to C1 | 1.00 ± 0.00 | 0.33 ± 0.06 | 0.75 ± 0.15 | M5 times the pinned price sheet | Estimate. I recall Haiku-tier at about one third of Sonnet-tier prices. Step 0 checks this. |
| M7 Reason grounded rate | 0.95 ± 0.04 | 0.90 ± 0.06 | 0.94 ± 0.04 | Opus judge, blind to config | Short reasons are easy to ground in the ticket. |
| M8 Configs meeting D6 | C1 yes | C2 no | C3 yes | `grade.mjs` checks R3 and R4 | This follows from M1 and M3. I predict C3 wins on cost. |

## Evaluate

**Files built.**
- `agent/triage.mjs` is the triage agent. It reads one ticket and returns JSON.
- `agent/prompts/zero-shot.md` and `agent/prompts/few-shot.md` hold the prompts.
- `spe/evals/data/r01/tickets.jsonl` holds the 120 eval tickets. `spe/evals/data/r01/gold.jsonl` holds the gold labels in a separate file.
- `spe/evals/data/dev/` holds the 20 dev tickets.
- `spe/evals/graders/grade.mjs`, `schema.mjs`, and `judge-prompt.md` are the graders.
- `spe/evals/harness/r01-workflow.js` is the Workflow script.

**Harness steps and gates.**

| Step | Action | Gate to pass |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | Preflight. I confirm pwd, git remote, and branch, and that `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is set. I print the name only. I read current model IDs and prices. | All match. Otherwise I halt and ask. |
| 1 | An Opus subagent writes the dev set, eval set, and gold labels from a label guide. You spot-check 10 gold labels if you want to. | Label counts cover every category. At least 15 tickets are gold P1. |
| 2 | I build the agent and prompts using the dev set only. | All 3 configs run on 3 dev tickets. |
| 3 | Grader selftest | The oracle (gold as predictions) scores 1.00. Empty output scores 0. Shuffled labels score at or below 0.25. |
| 4 | Control | No earlier round exists to regrade. Instead, I grade a fixed file with 10 known errors. It must score exactly 0.917 on M1 (110 of 120). |
| 5 | Dry run on 3 cells, one per config | The schema passes, costs are logged, and the peek scan runs clean. |
| 6 | Launch the Workflow | It returns at launch. I close out when the completion notice arrives. |

**Workflow rules.**
- One `ROUND = "r01"` constant. No round number is typed into prompt text.
- A cell is one config on one ticket. Each cell gets 2 trials. If the 2 trials disagree, the cell gets up to 2 more, with a cap of 4.
- Code checks run first. The Opus judge scores only R6.
- Trials get the ticket text only. They never get access to `gold.jsonl`, the graders, or `spe/predictions/`. The harness scans every transcript for those paths and voids any trial that touched them.
- The harness tracks spend after every trial. It skips any trial that would cross the cap and logs the skip.
- The run ends with failure analysis on every miss, then a completeness critic (Opus) that checks that every metric and config has a number.

**Workflow arguments.**
```json
{
  "ROUND": "r01",
  "configs": ["C1", "C2", "C3"],
  "tickets": "spe/evals/data/r01/tickets.jsonl",
  "trialsPerCell": 2,
  "maxTrialsPerCell": 4,
  "budgetUsd": 15,
  "maxConcurrency": 8,
  "judgeModel": "opus",
  "outDir": "spe/evals/results/r01/"
}
```

**Cost estimate (unmeasured).** About 720 base trials at about 1,000 tokens each, plus split-cell retries and judge calls. I estimate $3 to $6. The hard cap is $15.

## Order of work and local commits

1. Write `spe/spec/transcripts/2026-10-21-r01.md` with your prompt verbatim. Write `spe/spec/spec.md` and `spe/spec/disagreements.md`. Commit `SPE r01 specify: triage spec and defaults D1-D8`.
2. Copy this plan to `spe/plans/r01.md`. Write `spe/predictions/r01.yaml`. Its first line is `# Saved before the eval ran. Do not edit after the run.` It holds round, date 2026-10-21, author "Claude, approved by the user in plan mode", configs, pinned model IDs, each number with its band and Why, and `same_as_last_round: n/a`. Commit `SPE r01 predict: C3 meets the bar at about 0.75x C1 cost`.
3. Build the dataset, agent, graders, and Workflow script. Run gates 3 to 5. Commit `SPE r01 evaluate (harness): agent configs, graders, workflow`.
4. Launch the Workflow. When the completion notice arrives, commit the raw results as `SPE r01 evaluate (results): <headline>`.
5. Close out. Write `spe/prediction-log.md` with Metric, Config, Predicted, Measured, Same as last round, Verdict, and Closer. Under it, "Which Why broke" quotes each missed Why and names the wrong assumption. I say plainly if the naive guess beat my numbers. Write `spe/failures.md` with F-numbered failure types. Add a "Proposed for round r02" table to the spec. Write `spe/predictions/r02-draft.yaml` with `status: draft`. Write `spe/README.md`. Commit `SPE r01 learn: <headline>` and tag `spe-r01` locally.

## Halt conditions

I stop and report to you if any of these happen:
- Spend reaches the $15 cap.
- The peek scan finds a trial that read gold labels or predictions.
- The grader selftest or the control fails.
- A step needs one of your open decisions.

If all 3 configs pass every check, r02 needs harder tickets or stricter graders. The loop ends after 3 rounds in a row where predictions match results.
